steps.title: Same note, different sound
steps.text: Hoot and Bleep can sing exactly the same note. But they sound different. How can that be?

steps.title: Feel the wiggle
steps.text: Put a gentle hand on your throat and hum. Can you feel a buzz? Now stop. Sound is a wiggle that travels through the air.

wow.text: Sound is a wiggle in the air that travels all the way to your ears.

steps.dad: Hum together, quietly then loudly. Does the buzz stop when the humming stops?

steps.title: Square wiggles and pointy wiggles
steps.text: The robots' screens show their wiggles. Bleep's wiggle is square, like steps. Hoot's wiggle is pointy, like mountains.
steps.dad: Square waves are often called hollow. Triangle waves are softer and sweeter.

steps.prompt: Listen. Which shape made that sound?
steps.reveal: The triangle! Pointy wiggles make a soft, smooth sound.
Fizz's wiggles are all jumbled up. That makes a hissy sound. Old games used it for drums.

steps.title: A chip with four shapes
steps.text: This little chip made the sounds in an old computer called the Commodore 64. It could make all four of our shapes: triangle, saw, square and noise.

art.credit: SID sound chip. Photo: mariom990, public domain
art.alt: A black computer chip with metal legs

wow.text: It could play 3 sounds at once: a band of just three robots.

steps.intro: Bleep can make its squares skinny or fat. Tap each one. Do they sound different?

steps.title: Draw a sound, like a Game Boy
steps.text: The Game Boy had one sound you could draw yourself. It was made of 32 little steps. Our Wave Drawer has 32 steps too!

art.credit: Game Boy. Photo: Evan-Amos, public domain

wow.text: The Game Boy's wave had 32 steps, and each step could be one of 16 heights.

steps.intro: Draw your own wiggle with your finger, then press the pads. When you love it, give our robot a name and save it!

steps.title: Make rice dance
need: Cling film and an elastic band
A pan and a wooden spoon
steps: Stretch cling film tight over the bowl. Hold it on with the elastic band.
Sprinkle a little rice on top.
A grown-up bangs the pan close to the bowl. Watch the rice jump!
steps.why: The bang makes the air wiggle. The wiggles shake the cling film, like the eardrum inside your ear, and the rice dances.
steps.safety: Rice grains are small: keep them on the table and away from mouths. The grown-up does the banging.

debrief: Which sound shape do you like best?
What does our own robot sound like?
